# Vectros API — Integration Context

Vectros is the secure data, document, search, and AI back-end that developers
build apps on — a typed data store, a document pipeline, hybrid search,
citation-grounded retrieval, multi-tenant isolation, least-privilege access
control, and an audited compliance posture, behind one coherent API. The same
typed model is reachable both app-natively (typed SDKs for TypeScript, Python, and
Java; a forkable data-plane app and React toolkit) and agent-natively (an official
MCP server), with a CLI for provisioning.

The current surface spans: Documents and structured Records (with schema-defined
indexing, lookup/range queries, and folders), hybrid Search (BM25 + vector, RRF
fusion), grounded inference (chat, RAG, document-ask, model catalog), the
Identity plane (users, plus identity entities in any namespace — `org` and
`client` are reserved names, and you register any namespace before use), per-customer isolation
with scoped keys and app-contexts, read-access logging, GDPR erasure and export,
and billing/usage reporting.

## Recommended integration paths

Most integrations should NOT hand-roll HTTP. Reach for a client:

- **SDKs (`@vectros-ai/sdk` for TypeScript, plus Python and Java)** — the typed,
  recommended path for application code. All three are generated from the same spec
  that drives the API, so method names and types match it exactly. For TypeScript:
  `npm install @vectros-ai/sdk`, construct one client with a token and environment,
  then call sub-clients grouped by area (`records`, `schemas`, `documents`,
  `folders`, `search`, `inference`, `identity`, `auth`).
- **CLI (`@vectros-ai/cli`, `vectros`)** — provision from a terminal or CI:
  blueprints, app-contexts, identities, scoped keys, and a one-command MCP
  credential bootstrap (`npx -y @vectros-ai/cli bootstrap`). No code, no handling
  your root key directly.
- **MCP server (`@vectros-ai/mcp-server`)** — see below.

## MCP server — call Vectros as native agent tools

Vectros ships an official **Model Context Protocol** server
(`@vectros-ai/mcp-server`) that exposes the data plane to MCP-aware agents
(Claude Desktop, Cursor, Cline, Continue, VS Code, hosted platforms) as callable
tools — search, records, documents, folders, and grounded inference — with no
custom integration code. Drop one entry into the agent's MCP config:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "vectros": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@vectros-ai/mcp-server"],
      "env": { "VECTROS_API_KEY": "ssk_live_..." }
    }
  }
}
```

It is a thin shim over the SDK: tenant isolation and scope enforcement hold
exactly as on the API — running the server does not expand a credential's reach.
The tools are data-plane only (no web or third-party tools). Use a scoped
permanent key (`ssk_*`) for desktop installs; the CLI `bootstrap` mints one and
merges the config for you. Full details: https://docs.vectros.ai/guides/clients/mcp/

## Base URL & Auth

- **URL:** `https://api.vectros.ai/v1`
- **Auth:** `Authorization: Bearer <token>`
- **Root keys (`sk_live_*` / `sk_test_*`):** Long-lived, server-side only. Never
  expose in client-side code or agent prompts.
- **Scoped permanent keys (`ssk_*`):** Least-privilege keys carrying exactly the
  permissions you grant. The right shape for agents and MCP installs.
- **Scoped tokens (`st_*`):** Short-lived JWTs minted via `POST /v1/auth/token`.
  Use for client-side or per-session access. Scoped to specific resources and
  operations.

## Core Architecture & Execution Rules

1. **The Ingestion Split (Documents vs. Records):**
   - Unstructured data (PDFs, raw text): `POST /v1/documents`
   - Structured JSON data: define shape with `POST /v1/schemas`, then store and
     index with `POST /v1/records`
   - Numeric range (64-bit): every JSON number in a payload or search body must fall
     within the signed 64-bit integer range; an out-of-range number is rejected with
     `400`. Send large whole-number identifiers (account ids, external keys) as STRINGS,
     not numbers — a string field stores them exactly and supports exact-match lookup.

2. **The File Upload Handshake (CRITICAL — never skip this):**
   - Files are NOT sent as multipart/form-data to the API.
   - Step 1: `POST /v1/documents/upload` with filename and indexMode → get `uploadUrl`
   - Step 2: HTTP PUT the raw file bytes directly to `uploadUrl`
   - The system indexes automatically after the PUT completes.

3. **Hybrid Search (BM25 + Vector — RRF fusion):**
   - `POST /v1/search` fuses BM25 text scoring and semantic vector similarity via
     Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF). Always default to `mode: HYBRID`.
   - For exact phrase matching, set `textMode: PHRASE`.
   - For broad semantic-only queries, set `mode: SEMANTIC`.

4. **Context Hydration for LLMs (CRITICAL):**
   - Search returns `chunkText` (the exact matched snippet) and `contextText`
     (the broader surrounding passage).
   - Always feed `contextText` to LLM prompts. Using `chunkText` alone causes
     context fragmentation and degrades answer quality.

5. **The Identity Plane (users + namespaced entities):**
   - Two dimensions: users (`POST /v1/users`) and identity entities
     (`POST /v1/entities/{namespace}`). `org` and `client` are reserved
     namespace names — so an organization is `POST /v1/entities/org`. There
     are no `/v1/orgs` or `/v1/clients` routes. **Register both explicitly
     before use** (root key, same shape as registering your own namespace
     below, e.g. `{"namespace":"org","entityBacked":true,"specificityRank":1000}`
     and `client` at `specificityRank:2000`); `POST /v1/entities/org`/`client`
     returns `400` until you do. A one-time step per account; once
     registered, both work identically to any other namespace.
   - Register your own namespaces (`team`, `project`, …) with
     `POST /v1/namespaces` (`{"namespace":"team","entityBacked":true,"specificityRank":10}`,
     root key only). `specificityRank` is a required, account-unique integer position
     in your specificity order (breaks a tie when a caller holds two scope
     dimensions at once) — leave headroom (`10`, `20`, `30`, …) between values.
     `entityBacked` defaults to `false` — a false/unregistered namespace
     is a free-string scope value with no entities route, so set it `true` if you
     want entities. Entity-backed values are then existence-checked on write.
   - **Placement:** a registration is TENANT-WIDE by default (its entities are
     shared by every app context, same as `org`/`client`). Pass `?contextId=<id>`
     on `POST /v1/namespaces` to make it CONTEXT-OWNED instead: its entities
     live entirely inside that one app context, invisible to every other
     context, with no shared configuration. A registration's `contextId` is
     fixed once set and cannot be changed later. `?contextId=` then applies to
     every `/v1/entities/{namespace}` operation, not just creation (create,
     read, update, delete, versions, lookup): required for a context-owned
     namespace, rejected for a tenant-wide one.
   - **Idempotency:** both require an `externalId`. POSTing with an existing
     `externalId` safely returns the existing record — no 409 Conflict, safe to
     retry. Pass `?upsert=true` on an entity create to overwrite instead — that
     needs `entities:u:<namespace>` in addition to `entities:c:<namespace>`.

6. **Ownership is `scopes`, not `orgId`/`clientId`:**
   - Records, documents, folders, and schemas carry `scopes` — an array of
     `<namespace>:<value>` entries (e.g. `["org:<id>"]`), max two. There are no
     `orgId`/`clientId` fields anywhere; sending them is a 400. On an identity
     entity the same field holds its parents — max two, each in a namespace
     DIFFERENT from the entity's own (a parent edge always crosses namespaces).
   - Filter lists with `?scope=<namespace>:<value>` (one per query; pair with
     `?userId=` for both dimensions). In search and the RAG `search` block, use
     `"scope": "<namespace>:<value>"`.
   - Bind a credential with `scope:<namespace>` keys in a token's
     `dataScope`/`identity` and in an access profile's `identityOverrides`
     (e.g. `{"dataScope":{"scope:org":["<id>", null]}}` — the `null` additively
     grants tenant-level, owner-less rows). Reference the caller's own value
     with `${{ self.scope.<namespace> }}`.
   - Grant access with `entities:<verb>:<namespace>`, mirroring
     `records:<verb>:<type>`.

7. **Async Indexing & Webhooks:**
   - Document and record indexing is asynchronous. The resource is created
     immediately but `indexStatus` transitions PENDING_INDEX → INDEXED over seconds.
     INDEXED means keyword (TEXT) matching is immediate — the semantic (vector)
     leg is separately eventually-consistent, typically queryable a second or two
     later. A HYBRID/RAG query sharing keywords with a fresh item still surfaces
     it right away via the keyword leg; a query that can only match it
     semantically may not for those first few seconds.
     Indexing can also terminate in FAILED: a failed resource carries an
     `indexFailure` object with a typed `code` (`SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE`,
     `TEXT_INDEX_FAILED`, `EMBEDDING_FAILED`, `INDEXING_FAILED`,
     `VECTOR_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`, `INTERNAL`). When polling, treat FAILED as terminal —
     do not wait for INDEXED — and branch on `indexFailure.code`, not on message text.
   - Register webhooks to receive `document.indexed`, `document.failed`,
     `record.indexed`, `record.failed` events. The envelope's `data` carries
     `userId` and `scopes` when present — the same ownership spelling as REST — and,
     on the `.failed` events, the `indexFailure` object described above.
   - Webhook payloads are signed with HMAC-SHA256. Verify the
     `X-Vectros-Signature` header (`sha256=<hex>`), computed over the literal
     string `<X-Vectros-Timestamp>.<body>` keyed by the hex-decoded secret.

8. **Pagination:**
   - List, lookup, and version endpoints return a uniform cursor-paginated
     envelope: `{ data, nextCursor }`. Pass `nextCursor` back as the `startFrom`
     query param to fetch the next page; `null` means no more pages.
   - Two endpoints are NOT enveloped: `POST /v1/search` (read `results`) and
     `GET /v1/usage` (returns its payload directly). Search paging uses its own
     `limit` (1–100) plus an explicit `hasMore` boolean on the response — true
     when more results exist past this page. `totalResults` is an approximate
     matching-pool size, not a reliable paging signal; use `hasMore` instead.
   - A context-confined credential's `GET /v1/usage` sections (`credits`, `search`,
     `documents`, `records`, `identity`, `inference`, `readAccess`, `tenants`) narrow to
     that context alone — a root key or a cross-context credential still sees full-account
     totals. Two exceptions: `reads.calls.used`/`reads.dataOut.bytes` read `0` for a
     context-confined credential (metered per account, no per-context breakdown exists),
     and `credits.limit` always reflects your whole plan.

9. **Named platform capabilities (`granted_capabilities`):**
   - A scope clause (in a role, an access profile, or an invitation) accepts
     an optional `granted_capabilities` array alongside `allowed_actions` and
     `data_scope`. A capability grants a bounded, cross-context effect the
     `resource:ops` verb grammar cannot express on its own.
   - Four names are recognized in this release. `member-lifecycle`: create and
     remove identities in app contexts the credential can already reach.
     `forensic-read`: read the access log across every context in the tenant
     (adds to, does not replace, the `access-log:r` action). `context-directory-read`:
     read the tenant's app-context directory (contexts, roles, access
     profiles) and a principal's cross-context membership, across every
     context. `delegate-mint`: mint a scoped key (`POST /v1/admin/keys/scoped`)
     bound to a principal other than the caller.
   - The list is closed and versioned with the API. An absent or empty array
     grants nothing (silence, not a wildcard). An unrecognized name denies the
     WHOLE clause, including its `allowed_actions`, rather than being dropped.
     `"*"` in `allowed_actions` never confers a capability; name each one
     explicitly.

## Trust, isolation & compliance

- Every data-plane resource is partitioned by an auth-derived context that fails
  closed — lookups never cross a context boundary.
- Sensitive fields are destroyed at write time and kept out of the search index;
  read-time masking applies unless a caller is explicitly scoped to reveal.
- Read-access logging, GDPR-style erasure and export, and per-customer
  hard-delete are first-class operations.

## Documentation & Full Specification

- **No full corpus at this host.** `vectros.ai` serves only this `llms.txt`
  integration brief — there is **no `https://vectros.ai/llms-full.txt`** (don't
  request it; it 404s). The full documentation corpus lives on the docs host:
  **https://docs.vectros.ai/llms-full.txt**.
- **Docs home:** https://docs.vectros.ai/ — concept, how-to, and reference guides,
  plus a docs index for LLMs at https://docs.vectros.ai/llms.txt and the full
  corpus at https://docs.vectros.ai/llms-full.txt
- **Canonical OpenAPI spec:** https://docs.vectros.ai/openapi.yaml — OpenAPI 3.0.
  Never hallucinate endpoints or fields. Always refer to the spec for exact
  payload structures.
- **Rendered API reference:** https://docs.vectros.ai/api-reference/
